internal_provenance_note_csv_writing_bug.what_happened: task3_tail_census() in scripts/exact_threshold_analysis.py originally wrote its CSV/JSON outputs to fixed filenames regardless of which thresholds were passed. Calling it a second time for the 0.9999/0.99999 supplementary table silently overwrote SPA10M_EXACT_THRESHOLD_TAIL_CENSUS.csv and work/task3_tail_census.json with the supplementary-threshold numbers.
internal_provenance_note_csv_writing_bug.what_was_NOT_affected: No computed numerical result was ever wrong. The in-memory census dict for Harvey's two literal thresholds (0.9997/0.99997) was bound to a distinct Python variable before the second call ran, so this report, receipt.json's final_answers, and work/master_results.json were correct throughout -- only the two on-disk CSV/JSON files named above were transiently wrong.
internal_provenance_note_csv_writing_bug.how_caught: Noticed directly (identical SHA256 for two files that should differ) while regenerating SHA256SUMS, i.e. by the same file-integrity discipline this package's own adversarial-check culture requires -- not by a dedicated unit test.
internal_provenance_note_csv_writing_bug.fix: Parameterized task3_tail_census()'s output filenames (json_name/csv_name arguments) so the main-threshold and supplementary-threshold calls write to distinct files. Reran scripts/exact_threshold_analysis.py end-to-end; every number reproduced identically to the pre-fix in-memory values. Reran scripts/adversarial_self_check.py; all 6 checks pass against the corrected files.
internal_provenance_note_csv_writing_bug.current_state_verified: SPA10M_EXACT_THRESHOLD_TAIL_CENSUS.csv (0.9997/0.99997) and SPA10M_SUPPLEMENTARY_0P9999_0P99999.csv (0.9999/0.99999) are now confirmed distinct files (different SHA256) holding their own intended threshold rows.
